text.headline: Timeline of Austria
text.text: Major events in the history of Austria.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The earliest known settlements in what is now Austria date back to around 5000 BC, with evidence of farming communities in the region.

events.headline: Roman Conquest
events.text: The Romans conquered the region around 15 BC, establishing the province of Noricum, which became an important part of the Roman Empire.

events.headline: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: The fall of the Western Roman Empire in 476 AD led to the fragmentation of power in the region, with various tribes settling in Austria.

events.headline: Part of the Carolingian Empire
events.text: Austria became part of the Carolingian Empire under Charlemagne, which helped to spread Christianity and feudalism in the region.

events.headline: Duchy of Austria Established
events.text: The Duchy of Austria was officially established in 1156, marking the beginning of a distinct political entity in the region.

events.headline: Habsburg Dynasty Ascends
events.text: The Habsburgs gained control of Austria after the Battle of Dürnkrut, establishing a dynasty that would dominate European politics for centuries.

events.headline: Habsburgs Rule Bohemia and Hungary
events.text: Following the death of Louis II of Hungary, the Habsburgs expanded their influence by acquiring the crowns of Bohemia and Hungary.

events.headline: Thirty Years' War Begins
events.text: The Thirty Years' War began in 1618, significantly affecting Austria and leading to widespread devastation and political changes in Europe.

events.headline: Maria Theresa Becomes Ruler
events.text: Maria Theresa ascended to the throne in 1740, becoming the only female ruler of the Habsburg dominions and implementing significant reforms.

events.headline: Austrian Empire Established
events.text: The Austrian Empire was officially proclaimed in 1804, marking a new phase in the Habsburg's political structure amidst the Napoleonic Wars.

events.headline: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
events.text: The Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867 created the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary, significantly altering the political landscape of Central Europe.

events.headline: Start of World War I
events.text: World War I began in 1914 following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, leading to the eventual collapse of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

events.headline: End of the Austro-Hungarian Empire
events.text: The Austro-Hungarian Empire dissolved in 1918 after World War I, leading to the establishment of the First Austrian Republic.

events.headline: Anschluss with Nazi Germany
events.text: In 1938, Austria was annexed by Nazi Germany in a political union known as the Anschluss, leading to significant social and political upheaval.

events.headline: End of World War II
events.text: World War II ended in 1945, resulting in Austria being occupied by Allied forces and later declared a neutral country.

events.headline: Austrian State Treaty
events.text: The Austrian State Treaty was signed in 1955, restoring Austria's sovereignty and declaring its permanent neutrality.

events.headline: Austria Joins the European Union
events.text: Austria became a member of the European Union in 1995, marking a significant step in its integration into European political and economic structures.

events.headline: Adoption of the Euro
events.text: Austria adopted the Euro as its official currency in 2002, replacing the Austrian schilling and further integrating into the European economy.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted Austria in 2020, leading to lockdowns, economic challenges, and public health measures.

events.headline: Political Changes
events.text: In 2021, Austria saw significant political changes, including the resignation of Chancellor Sebastian Kurz amid corruption allegations.
